summary: Pasang Wangdu specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. Supervised by Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner, he served as a professor at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2006–2014).

Pascale Haag is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1996–2002) and at Paris Nanterre University (~2013–2018). She held a post at the École des hautes études en sciences sociales around 2003.

Pascale Hugon works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and taught Flavio A. Geisshuesler.

Pataraporn Sirikanchana is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania and served as a professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).

Patrice Ladwig works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Münster, University of Edinburgh, and EHESS, and held positions at the University of Bristol and the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

Patricia Berger works in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley, studied under Mark C. Elliott and Steven D. Goodman, curated at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco, and joined UC Berkeley's faculty in 1996.

Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and Sinologist. Educated at Chicago (1968) and Columbia (1970, 1975), she held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1975–1997), the Institute for Advanced Study (1998), and the University of Washington (1997).

Patricia Fister specializes in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Kansas, where she was assistant professor of art history (~1985–1991), before becoming a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~2001–2019).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani works in Sinology and Tibetology. She completed graduate study at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zumo Zhou, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Perry Link.

Patrick Jory is a historian who studied at the University of Western Australia (~1985–1989) and completed his PhD at the Australian National University (~1991–1996) under Craig J. Reynolds. He held a post at the University of Queensland (~2011).

Patrick McAllister works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2005–2011), where he was supervised by Helmut Krasser and taught by Karin Preisendanz and Ernst Steinkellner.

Indologist and religious studies scholar Patrick Olivelle studied at Oxford (~1968–1972) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1972–1974). He served as chairman at Indiana University (~1984–1991) and Chair of Asian Studies at the University of Texas at Austin (1991).
Patrick Pranke is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.
Patrick R. Uhlmann works in Buddhist studies. He was a PhD candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles (attested 2012), where he studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Pattaratorn Chirapravati specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Cornell (~1988–1994), held posts at Sonoma State and the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (1997–2002), and became an associate professor at California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016).
Paul B. Courtright specializes in religious studies and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and Emory University (attested 1998).

Paul B. Donnelly works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa and traditional teachers Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe and Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Bernard specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne (through 1983) and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1980–1997).

Paul Carus was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Hermann Grassmann, held a post at Open Court Publishing Company (~1887–1919), and taught Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki.

Paul Copp is a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UMass Amherst and Princeton (PhD attested 2005). He held posts at Heidelberg Academy of Sciences (2006), Western Michigan University, and the University of Chicago (attested 2014).
